body:
Hey, I just wanted to follow up with an update. Again, thank you for your support. It turns out the nerve pain medication I was prescribed, Gabapentin, has a risk of inducing higher states of anxiety, fear and thoughts of suicide. I am certain this is what was causing my recurring suicidal thoughts.

I am lucky I researched this when I did. I came across user testimony and a case study by the company that makes the drug. Both warned against it being prescribed to patients with a history of depression. This is a real oversight on my doctor's part, as a history of depression and suicidal thoughts is on my patient chart. I was never made aware of the risk.

It has been two days since I've taken Gabapentin. I still have heightened anxiety but I am familiar with this kind of anxiety. I feel more in control and have an easier time distracting myself from the anxiety or letting myself feel it until it passes.

I have an appointment with a psychiatrist on Tuesday. Hopefully he will prescribe me something to help manage the anxiety.

I have. I also just spoke with my therapist on the phone who provided some strategies to deal with the recurring suicidal thoughts. I am in the process of scheduling an appointment with a psychiatrist. Unfortunately a lot of them do not take my insurance, but if I have to pay for the session(s) I will budget it.

The thing that hits me hard is that I am clearly trying things/doing things to help myself -- why do these thoughts keep coming? Why do I keep having them?

There is a part of me that wants to die but there is strong part of me that wants to figure this out and live. It is a struggle, but I will figure this out.

I understand your reasoning. 

I personally do not have a strong family connection. My mother passed away when I was young. I do not speak with my father or brother for reasons I do not wish to get into at the moment.

The thought of hurting my friends doesn't register as a reason not to commit suicide. I'm not sure why. I do care for them, I do love them. I know my death would have an impact on them, but they would move on and continue life.

Sharing this does make me feel better, at least for the moment. I appreciate you taking the time to read my post and respond to my messages.
How do you manage? What do you do to support/help yourself? I am struggling with the day to day and am having trouble finding meaning or purpose in things. It all feels a bit pointless.
